What it is

MarineOmega®

Omega-3 fatty acids have to come from food because the body does not make them itself. The main source is fish, and many people do not eat fish often enough. MarineOmega is made as a practical way to add EPA and DHA.

Besides fish oil, it contains krill oil. According to Nu Skin material, the EPA and DHA in krill oil come in phospholipid form, and krill oil also carries the antioxidant astaxanthin. According to the same material, four softgels provide about 1,200 mg of pure omega-3.

Who it suits

Adults who rarely eat fish and want to add EPA and DHA. If you are allergic to fish or shrimp, do not use it, because it contains both.

FAQ

Common questions

What are EPA and DHA?

Both are omega-3 fatty acids. According to Nu Skin material, they are building blocks of many cells and tissues in the body, found in large amounts in the brain and retina.

How is it different from regular fish oil?

MarineOmega adds krill oil, which carries EPA and DHA in phospholipid form and the antioxidant astaxanthin. According to Nu Skin material, a bottle holds twice as many fish oil softgels as Optimum Omega.

Can I take it?

According to Nu Skin material, it can be taken at the recommended dose and its fish and krill sources are tested to be free of toxins, contaminants and heavy metals through the Pharmanex quality process. Still follow the allergy and surgery warnings above.

Can I get all my omega-3 from food alone?

People who eat fish every day can get most of what they need. But because of concerns about pollutants, some fish are advised in limited amounts, so a supplement is a practical way to add to your intake.

Why is the fishy taste reduced?

The softgel is vanilla-scented and uses natural lemon oil, which Nu Skin material says helps reduce the fishy taste.
